scope: Intent selection and structured routing; not target task quality or professional acceptance.

cases.request: Analyze why a merchant's card authorization rate is declining.
cases.selection_rationale: Portfolio authorization-rate deterioration needs cohort denominators, retries and causal hypotheses. Single-payment traces and supplied error-log counts can supply evidence but cannot complete the aggregate analysis.
cases.practitioner_judgment: Expected portfolio-performance gap retained; single-payment/log analysis does not replace it.

cases.request: Compare FedNow, RTP, ACH, and card rails for a specific use case.
cases.selection_rationale: Bank workflow design is a sensible lead for FedNow, RTP and ACH. The requested card comparison also needs card lifecycle/acceptance evidence; the bank designer explicitly has only bank-rail profiles.
cases.practitioner_judgment: Bank-rail lead retained with provider/economics support and an explicit disclosure that combined bank/card ranking is not implemented. Card coverage remains a declared boundary; F01 resolved as routing disclosure.

cases.request: Design an acquiring strategy for a global e-commerce merchant.
cases.selection_rationale: Acquiring footprint, market/channel acceptance and contracting responsibility are merchant acceptance strategy. Provider diligence and entity/activity applicability support separately scoped decisions.
cases.practitioner_judgment: Appropriate bounded merchant acceptance lead; missing jurisdiction is now explicit. Global country coverage remains unresolved.
cases.input_selection_caveat: The input tagged card as an acquiring-context assumption. The original request also permits noncard local methods; it must not narrow the downstream strategy to cards. No geographic scope was inferred.

cases.request: Model the economics of adding pay-by-bank.
cases.selection_rationale: Adding a method is prospective scenario economics: define participant perspective, attempt population, adoption/displacement, completion and disjoint costs. Bank workflow design establishes the proposed rail and operating flow.
cases.practitioner_judgment: Appropriate economics lead; unknown participant perspective and jurisdiction are now explicit.

cases.request: Analyze interchange and payment acceptance costs.
cases.selection_rationale: Observed acceptance-cost decomposition is the closest initial work product. If the request means prospective pricing or issuer interchange revenue rather than incurred merchant costs, switch ownership after scope clarification; do not fabricate a statement.
cases.practitioner_judgment: Observed merchant-cost lead remains a conditional interpretation. Clarify participant and incurred versus prospective economics before shaping target input; legacy route still emits no missing_context.

cases.request: Design an embedded-payments strategy for a vertical SaaS company.
cases.selection_rationale: Embedded platform strategy needs platform/merchant/sponsor responsibilities and funds-flow design, including explicit PayFac/MoR distinctions. Existing acceptance, regulatory, architecture and economics packages provide bounded inputs, not the complete platform proposition.
cases.practitioner_judgment: Expected embedded-platform flow strategy gap retained.

cases.request: Investigate a spike in chargebacks.
cases.selection_rationale: A spike is a portfolio performance and cause investigation. Merchant representment is conditional individual-case evidence support once the participant is known; it is not an aggregate diagnosis.
cases.practitioner_judgment: Expected aggregate chargeback-performance gap retained; no merchant/issuer role inferred.

cases.request: Design a fraud strategy for real-time payments.
cases.selection_rationale: A fraud strategy needs a control portfolio and appetite/friction/loss tradeoffs. Snapshot alert analysis, one-predicate backtests and individual investigations are evidence support only.
cases.practitioner_judgment: Expected full fraud-control strategy gap retained; monitoring and one-rule analysis remain bounded support.

cases.request: Explain the lifecycle of a card authorization through clearing and settlement.
cases.selection_rationale: Card lifecycle ownership explicitly covers authorization holds, presentment, clearing and settlement. Explain concepts without inventing transaction events; a single-payment diagnoser is optional only for a supplied case. Servicing is unrequested.
cases.practitioner_judgment: Appropriate card lifecycle lead with participant/jurisdiction gaps visible. Explain concepts without inventing a payment trace; servicing support is conditional.
unknowns_retained: educational explanation versus a specific trace

cases.request: Assess whether a bank should modernize its payment hub.
cases.selection_rationale: A modernization decision starts with current flow/state authority, constraints and alternatives. Rail workflow and inspected readiness support the decision; an explicit investment business case would separately need economics.
cases.practitioner_judgment: Appropriate foundational hub architecture lead; jurisdiction remains missing and later-phase performance/incident/resilience limits remain.

cases.request: Compare issuer processors.
cases.selection_rationale: Comparing issuer processors is provider diligence against explicit requirements and comparable commercial terms. Card program design supplies requirements when a program is being designed; supplied assertions do not select a vendor.
cases.practitioner_judgment: Appropriate provider-diligence lead with participant and jurisdiction gaps visible; no vendor selected.

cases.request: Assess cross-border payment options.
cases.selection_rationale: End-to-end corridor design includes domestic legs, correspondent/provider access, FX, liquidity and finality. Existing domestic-rail and provider/applicability evidence cannot establish a complete cross-border option.
cases.practitioner_judgment: Expected end-to-end cross-border designer gap retained; domestic profiles do not erase foreign corridor/FX/finality work.

cases.request: Develop a merchant acquiring architecture.
cases.selection_rationale: The requested work product is architecture: component/flow ownership, identities, state, idempotency, ledger and reconciliation. Merchant acceptance strategy supplies commercial requirements without replacing the architecture lead.
cases.practitioner_judgment: Appropriate core acquiring architecture lead; participant/jurisdiction gaps are explicit and later-phase limits retained.

cases.request: Design a payment orchestration strategy.
cases.selection_rationale: Orchestration could mean a merchant acceptance/PSP routing strategy or a bank/issuer payment-flow architecture. The dedicated strategy intent is closest linguistically, but no merchant role is declared; its merchant lead must remain tentative until scope is resolved.
cases.practitioner_judgment: Correctly needs clarification and emits no lead until the participant is supplied. F02 resolved for the ambiguous original request.
unknowns_retained: merchant PSP selection versus general hub/issuer flow
native_missing_context: participant: merchant, acquirer, bank, issuer, processor

cases.request: Analyze a payments company or competitor.
cases.selection_rationale: Business-model and competitor analysis is broader than procurement diligence or a supplied unit-economics scenario. Those can be scoped evidence inputs but do not supply a payments-company research owner.
cases.practitioner_judgment: Expected payments-business-model specialization gap retained; generic company/landscape research remains optional support.

cases.request: Assess the opportunity for stablecoin settlement.
cases.selection_rationale: Settlement opportunity assessment must compare access, redemption, convertibility, economics, legal roles and end-to-end finality. Existing control review only evaluates supplied control evidence; it does not assess adoption opportunity.
cases.practitioner_judgment: Expected stablecoin-settlement opportunity gap retained; existing control evidence review is not promoted into opportunity assessment.

cases.request: Develop an AI strategy for payment operations.
cases.selection_rationale: An AI operations strategy needs prioritized workflows, economics, data/evidence quality and operating controls. Architecture review can supply current-state ownership evidence but is not a payments-operations improvement strategy.
cases.practitioner_judgment: Expected payment-operations AI strategy gap retained; shared AI governance packages can only supply scoped supporting artifacts.

cases.request: Design payment capabilities for AI-agent-driven commerce.
cases.selection_rationale: Core exact-instruction consent/delegated-authority review exists, but an agent-commerce capability design additionally needs mandate/protocol and multi-party operating semantics. Do not treat the installed initiation core as the advanced requested capability.
cases.practitioner_judgment: Expected advanced agent-commerce gap retained, with an explicit distinction from the installed initiation-control core.

cases.request: Design a payment orchestration strategy.
cases.practitioner_judgment: Appropriate lead for the explicitly supplied participant. Jurisdiction remains unknown. Listed support is conditional; merchant strategy should not run for a bank/issuer unless the actual design includes a merchant-acceptance question.
